clue.text: Drug favoured by a police department

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of a British police force

explanation.surface: A narcotic said to be popular with a detective squad.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force; 'favoured by' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid is slang for the hallucinogen LSD.

clue.text: Damage caused by one married couple

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: Harm brought about by a single wedded duo.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or harm it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Coach for quartet being acted upon

parts.note: a quartet is four
a matter in hand is one being dealt with

explanation.surface: A trainer for a group of four musicians currently in action.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-in-hand is a carriage drawn by four horses driven by one person.

clue.text: Nuclear art form since lacking regularity

indicators.note: every other letter is lacking, so the letters kept come at regular intervals through these words

explanation.surface: Atomic art has been irregular ever since it began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking regularity' removes the regular, alternate letters, leaving the first, third, fifth and so on of ART FORM SINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear and atomic both describe energy or weapons from splitting or fusing atoms.

clue.text: A right racket — one in south American island!

indicators.note: in says the next pieces sit inside the abbreviation for South American

parts.note: a din is a loud racket
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a real commotion on a South American island.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places the island in South America, but 'south American' is just the abbreviation wrapping the other pieces; the island is in the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardinia is a large Italian island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Gamble on a letter to the Greeks

parts.note: to gamble is to bet

explanation.surface: Putting a wager on a letter sent to Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Raising some broncos — outrivalled by expert!

indicators.note: Raising says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rodeo rider rearing up some wild horses, beaten by a professional.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Raising' reads the hidden run OSOUTRIV upwards. The draft's definition 'by expert' is cut to 'expert': 'by' only links, since 'by expert' cannot stand for the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a person of outstanding skill, especially a performer.

clue.text: Butted in, set on pride being restored

indicators.note: something restored is put back together, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Interrupted, with one's self-respect being repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpose is to intervene or interject, so butting in is a past-tense match.

clue.text: Role that finds a compiler in company

indicators.note: in places the next letters within the abbreviation for company

parts.note: the setter of the crossword, the compiler, refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A part in a play landed by a crossword setter in a theatre troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter often calls themselves 'compiler', meaning ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a small but distinctive part in a film or play.

clue.text: Writer who changes it and hides fury

indicators.note: hides says the shuffled letters wrap round and conceal the word for fury
changes says the letters of the two short words are put into a new order

parts.note: fury is rage

explanation.surface: An author who alters his work and conceals his anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' shuffles IT AND into T-DIAN, which 'hides' the fury word in its middle. 'Writer' is fair: a tragedian can be an author of tragedies as well as an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an author of tragedies (also an actor in them).

clue.text: Return to help with little weight plan

indicators.note: Return says the word for help is turned to read backwards

parts.note: help is aid
a gram is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Going back to assist with a lightweight scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a schematic drawing, a kind of plan.

clue.text: Conscript launching vessel into river

indicators.note: into says the vessel goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a raft is a simple floating vessel

explanation.surface: An army recruit pushing off a boat into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a British river, a crossword favourite; 'launching' is surface colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is someone called up for compulsory military service.

clue.text: Champion new flyer

parts.note: a champion is a hero

explanation.surface: A winning pilot who has just started out.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged wading bird, so a creature that flies.

clue.text: Vehicle in which husband has complete skill

parts.note: over means finished, complete
craft is skill

explanation.surface: A car in which a married man shows total mastery.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovercraft is a craft riding on a cushion of air over land or water.

clue.text: Fruit dish Paul at once failed to finish

indicators.note: to dish is to ruin or wreck, so these letters are broken up and rearranged
the phrase stops short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Paul couldn't finish a plate of food straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed to finish' drops the last E of PAUL AT ONCE; 'dish' then rearranges the remaining nine letters. 'dish' looks like a plate but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantaloup is a variety of melon with orange flesh.

clue.text: Expect head to support prank on one

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath the others
in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: an antic is a playful trick
one is the Roman numeral I
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: Bracing oneself for the boss to back a practical joke on somebody.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate is to foresee or look forward to something.

clue.text: Rude parts of mathematics?

parts.note: read as crude bits of maths, it points to the common fractions with numerator over denominator, whose name contains a word for coarse

explanation.surface: Off-colour bits of a maths lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Common fractions such as three quarters are called by a name whose first word also means coarse.

clue.text: Praise a union for finding narcotic

parts.note: to praise is to laud
NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: Commending a trade union for discovering a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, Britain's coal miners' union.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudanum is a tincture of opium, once widely used as a sedative drug.

clue.text: One takes the lead and shoots sailor

parts.note: a director shoots, or films, scenes
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a leash and fires at a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen celebrity plays the leading role in movies.

clue.text: Song and drinks — the Spanish have a young leader!

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: a leader is a word's first letter

explanation.surface: A tune and a round of drinks, with the Spaniards fronted by a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundelay is a short simple song with a refrain.

clue.text: Nodding acquaintances

parts.note: taken literally, people you know who nod along to whatever the boss says, rather than people barely known

explanation.definitionFit: Sycophants who always agree are compliant followers.

clue.text: Lots of people argue in the civil defence

indicators.note: in places the word for argue inside the abbreviation

parts.note: CD is the abbreviation for civil defence
to row is to quarrel

explanation.surface: A mob disputing inside the emergency services.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd is a large gathering of folk.

clue.text: Part of America where there's gold, say — nothing new!

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
say means for example, abbreviated eg
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A region of the US with gold deposits but nothing fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is a state in the Pacific Northwest of the USA.

clue.text: Argues about working in a ship

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: in places the word for working inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
on means operating, working

explanation.surface: Debates going on concerning work aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason with someone is to argue logically, matching the verb.

clue.text: Cereal found in open topped vessels

indicators.note: having the top taken off, the word for vessels loses its first letter

parts.note: boats are vessels

explanation.surface: Breakfast grain discovered in bowls without lids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open topped' removes the first letter of BOATS; 'found in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a grain crop, eaten as porridge.

clue.text: Meals that need stimulants after starter of soup

indicators.note: after says the stimulants come behind the starter letter
the starter of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: uppers are stimulant drugs

explanation.surface: Dinners that need pick-me-ups following the soup course.
explanation.definitionFit: Suppers are evening meals.

clue.text: Locate quote in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is identified by how it is heard

parts.note: to quote is to cite

explanation.surface: Finding a line to recite at a casting call.
explanation.definitionFit: To site something is to place or position it.

clue.text: Prevent oxidisation with art works in iron

indicators.note: in places the oxidisation and the reworked art inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
rust is iron oxide formed by oxidisation

indicators.note: works means the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Stopping corrosion on metal with artistic treatments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges ART into RAT. 'oxidisation' looks like the start of a chemistry definition, but it is just a synonym piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To frustrate a plan is to thwart or block it.

clue.text: Test not unknown for fish

indicators.note: not says the unknown letter is to be left out

parts.note: a tryout is a test or trial
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: An exam that isn't a mystery for a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra x, y and z are unknowns, so 'unknown' gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater game fish.
